messages:
evan: heads up — during int8 calibration for the Gemma-converted Mistral run I started seeing repeated pad-like tokens and downstream kv-cache desyncs. full run -> small sample logs below. not sure if this is tokenizer mismatch or a quant rounding/overflow in the embedding layer.

jess: can you paste the exact conversion/quant commands and a minimal repro? curious if this happens pre-quant or only after int8 offline calibration.

evan: repro steps:
1) convert Mistral checkpoint with tools/convert_mistral_to_gemma.py --vocab mistral_vocab.json --out gemma.safetensors
2) build int8 calib with tools/calibrate.py --model gemma.safetensors --bits 8 --calib-steps 5000 --out gemma.int8
3) run small eval harness: python tools/eval_cache_smoke.py --model gemma.int8 --prompt-file tests/prompt_subset.txt

logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-20 14:02:03] token_lookup: token " the" -> id 50256
[2026-03-20 14:02:03] embed_idx: embedding index computed 128 for id 50256
[2026-03-20 14:02:03] kv_insert: inserting kv at pos 0 for token id 128
[2026-03-20 14:02:03] decode: emitted token id 50256 -> <|pad|> (repeated)
```
behavior: token ids from tokenizer (50k+) seem to be remapped to small indices (<=256) before kvcache insertion. observed when running int8 calibrated model, not when running fp16 converted checkpoint.

omar: weird. could it be an off-by-one in the vocab remapping step in converter? we saw similar mapping when switching from bpe->merged tokens before. did you check the converter's tokenmap file?

evan: yes checked tokenmap.json produced by conversion. it looks sane for most tokens but a contiguous block at high ids shows values like 0..255. snippet: `... "50250": 10, "50251": 11, "50252": 12, "50256": 128, ...` — which is exactly where the mismatch shows. i don't see that mapping in the original vocab.

rachel: could be a dtype/overflow when serializing tokenmap to int8 during the calibrate step? maybe a cast trimmed high ids to int8. bench-bot: caljob run attached? @bench-bot what was the last write type for tokenmap?

bench-bot: caljob/3732100987 completed, artifact tokenmap.bin written with dtype=int8 (size 256).

jess: AH — there we go. converter emits tokenmap.json with full int32 ids, but calibrate script was writing a compact tokenmap.bin and incorrectly using np.int8 when saving indices to reduce size. result: any id >127 wraps negative then cast to 0..255 on unsigned write. that explains the remap to small indices.

evan: ugh. that matches. to confirm — i reran calibrate with a forced tokenmap dtype int32 and the smoke eval no longer showed repeated pads. results look identical to fp16 run so far.

omar: fix path: update calibrate.py -> utils/io.py line ~142 to use dtype=np.int32 when persisting tokenmap.bin and add a sanity check that token ids in tokenmap are monotonically increasing/within xrange of vocab size. file a tiny PR and tag me for review.

jess: also add a CI smoke: run convert+calibrate+eval on a small vocab subset and assert no kvcache index wraps. keeps us from regressing.

evan: filing PR now. adding test. removing int8 tokenmap compaction until we implement robust compact encoding (with metadata). will push hotfix to staging.

rachel: nice catch. can we add a short note to onboarding checklist for new converters: ensure tokenmap save/load dtype preserved. put in docs/devex/converters.md?

evan: yup will add.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for branch fix/int8-tokenmap-fix -> staging at 2026-03-20T14:15:00Z :rocket:

jess: follow-up items: 1) audit other calibrate artifacts for accidental dtype compaction, 2) run a sweep of models converted in last 30 days for tokenmap.bin artifact dtype, 3) add end-to-end test for tokenmap fidelity across convert->calibrate->serve.

evan: noted. i'll kick off sweep and create tickets. thanks team :thumbsup:
